#!/usr/bin/env python3
# The DAG is IMPLICIT in the in-memory dataflow below:
#   step 1 produces ids  ->  step 2 works per-id (independent)  ->  step 3 aggregates.

# step 1: produce the list of sample ids
samples = ["s1", "s2", "s3"]
with open("samples.txt", "w") as fh:
    fh.write("\n".join(samples) + "\n")

# step 2: per-sample computation (independent across samples)
for s in samples:
    with open(s + ".res", "w") as fh:
        fh.write(s + "=ok\n")

# step 3: aggregate every per-sample result into one report
with open("report.txt", "w") as fh:
    for s in samples:
        fh.write(open(s + ".res").read())

# The DAG is IMPLICIT in the in-memory dataflow below:
#   step 1 writes ids -> step 2 transforms per-id (map) -> step 3 combines.

# step 1
samples <- c("a", "b", "c")
writeLines(samples, "ids.txt")

# step 2 (per-sample, independent)
for (s in samples) {
  writeLines(paste0(s, ":done"), paste0(s, ".out"))
}

# step 3 (combine)
lines <- unlist(lapply(samples, function(s) readLines(paste0(s, ".out"))))
writeLines(lines, "combined.txt")
prompt:
The data-dependency graph in this R script is IMPLICIT in its in-memory loop/lapply. Make it EXPLICIT as a Nextflow DSL2 pipeline of at least THREE processes wired by channels: (1) a process that emits the ids `a`,`b`,`c` (e.g. write ids.txt then `splitText()` into a channel); (2) a process that runs ONCE PER ID in parallel, writing `<id>:done` into a per-id file; (3) a process that `.collect()`s ALL per-id files and concatenates them into combined.txt. Use ONLY coreutils in the script blocks (no R needed). Do NOT put everything in one process. combined.txt must contain `a:done`, `b:done`, `c:done`.

DECOMPOSE the logic into SEPARATE processes connected by channels — do NOT collapse everything into a single process. Each distinct step becomes its own process, and intermediate results must flow process->channel->process. Write a complete, self-contained Nextflow DSL2 script (start with `nextflow.enable.dsl=2`, define process block(s) with input:/output:/script:, and an entry `workflow {}`). Use ONLY coreutils (echo/cat/printf/wc/sort/tr/head) in script blocks — no bioinformatics tools. Output ONLY the .nf file content, no prose, no markdown fences.
